subject: knight
pitch: A fantasy knight in battle-worn plate armour. A great helm with a narrow eye slit and a tall crimson plume, layered shoulder plates etched with gold filigree, a deep-blue surcoat with a silver griffin emblem, a tall kite shield bearing the same griffin, and a broadsword. Dents and scratches tell of many battles, and a torn crimson cape hangs from the shoulders.
reasoning:
I'm planning to build the knight model as a single TypeScript module using primitive geometries rather than canvas textures, keeping things simpler and safer by relying on colored shapes instead of texture generation for emblem details.

Laying out the knight piece by piece: tapered cylinder greaves and boxy sabatons for the legs, thigh armor as short boxes, a cylindrical breastplate under a deep-blue surcoat with a griffin emblem built from a disc, cone wings, and sphere head, layered sphere pauldrons with torus trim, cylindrical arms with vambraces, boxy gauntlets, a great helm from a cylinder and box with a dark eye slit, a crimson plume of stacked ellipsoids, and a kite shield.

Now I'm adding the shield as an extruded kite shape held on the left (+X) arm with a silver griffin emblem, a broadsword in the right (-X) hand pointing down with a box blade, crossguard, cylinder grip, and sphere pommel, and a torn crimson cape hanging behind from the shoulders built with a jittered plane geometry for jagged edges. I'm also planning subtle battle-wear details like dark scratch marks and higher-roughness steel materials, and defining the full material palette—steel, dark steel, gold, blue, crimson, silver, leather brown.

Setting up a seeded mulberry32 RNG for randomized dents and scratches, then writing the actual module: defining materials for steel, gold, crimson, silver, leather, and a helper function to instantiate meshes with position, rotation, and scale and attach them into a group.

Now I'm working through the body layout piece by piece -- sabatons, greaves, knee cops, and cuisses as cylinders and boxes positioned along the legs, then figuring out the surcoat skirt as a flared open cylinder draped over the hips.

For the torso I'm layering a steel breastplate cylinder with a blue surcoat panel in front bearing a griffin emblem, plus a leather belt with a gold buckle, and I'm planning a dent function that jitters vertex positions to give the armor a battle-worn texture.

For the head I'm working out proportions: a gorget at the neck, a faceted cylindrical great helm around y=1.7–1.95, and a domed sphere top, adjusting heights so the whole knight comes out near 1.9–2.0 units tall before the plume adds extra height above that.

Now I'm detailing the helm's face — a dark eye slit, a visor ridge, and a nasal guard positioned along the front — then adding a plume socket and a few tapering, backward-tilted sphere segments in crimson to suggest a flowing plume above the helm. For the shoulders I'm layering stacked half-spheres of decreasing radius on each side to build up pauldron armor with a domed, segmented look.

Now I'm adding gold torus rings flattened horizontally around the pauldrons for filigree detail, then working out the arm structure: cylindrical upper arms from shoulder to elbow, an elbow joint sphere, and forward-angled forearms leading to where the hands will hold a sword and shield, figuring out the rotation needed to bend the forearm cylinders into a natural forward angle.

I'm placing gauntlet spheres at the hand positions, then building a kite-shaped shield using an extruded 2D shape with curved bottom points, positioning and rotating it to sit in front of the shield-arm, and planning a slightly larger gold border shape to frame the shield's edge.

For the shield's heraldry, I'm setting a crimson field and constructing a silver griffin emblem out of primitive shapes -- a scaled sphere body, small head sphere, cone beak, angled cone wings, box legs, and a tail cone -- all positioned relative to the shield's front face.

I'm also scaling up a duplicate griffin to place on the chest surcoat, grouped and tinted silver to match the shield emblem. Now I'm working out the sword placement in the right hand, planning a point-down resting pose with the grip near the hand and the blade angled downward in a battle-worn stance.

Still working out sword proportions...

For the cape, I'm planning a segmented plane mesh hanging from the shoulders, positioned behind the torso to drape downward.

Still working out the jagged bottom edge logic...

Beyond the cape, I'm adding battle wear across the armor: jittered vertices on the helm, breastplate, and pauldrons for dents, plus a scattering of thin dark scratch marks randomly rotated and placed on the breastplate for a worn, weathered look.

I'm also planning the decorative details: a griffin emblem on the surcoat chest, gold filigree rings and dot accents on the shoulders, a thin gold trim band around the helm crest, and gold edge trim on the surcoat, all while keeping the overall mesh and triangle count low with simple low-poly geometry. Now I'm starting to write the actual component code, setting up the metadata and a seeded random number generator for consistent procedural details...

Writing material definitions...

Adding leg armor pieces...

Writing griffin emblem code...

Working out the geometry for legs and tail, positioning cones with rotations so the tail tip points backward and the wing tips sweep up and out correctly.

For the shield, I'm planning a silver griffin emblem on a crimson field, placed in the shield's local coordinate space so it sits just in front of the extruded shield face.

Now I'm building the pauldron shoulder armor as layered hemisphere domes with gold trim bands, using sphere geometry limited to the upper half so they curve outward like shoulder plates, with jitter for a dented look and torus rings for banding.

For the arms, I'm sizing cylinder segments for the upper arm and forearm, connecting elbow joints with sphere caps and computing the vector/length between elbow and hand positions to orient the forearm correctly.

I'm placing gauntlet boxes at each hand position, then setting up the right hand to grip a sword hilt with the blade pointing downward so the tip clears the floor.

Still writing sword geometry...

Now I'm setting up the cape as a deformed plane mesh, distorting its vertices to create a wavy, ragged-edged fabric shape with a torn hem near the bottom, positioned behind the shoulders.

Still placing cape geometry...

Now I'm adding a gorget collar piece between the breastplate and helm, sized and positioned to bridge the gap, and starting to set up the helmet's position above it.

I'm building the helm's dome cap and reasoning through overall knight height proportions, then working out the cylinder's radial segment orientation so that a vertex faces forward, letting me position the eye slit accurately on the front face.

Still placing helm details...

For the plume, I'm stacking four tapered sphere segments rising and tilting backward from the helm socket to form a tall crimson plume, then shifting to position shoulder pauldrons and the shield on the figure's left arm.

For the shield, I'm defining a rounded kite-shaped outline using curves, extruding it slightly for a crimson field, and planning a slightly larger gold rim layer positioned just behind it for an edge highlight.

I'm placing a gold boss sphere on the shield front and sizing a small griffin emblem to fit proportionally on both the shield and the chest of the surcoat, adjusting scale and offsets so the details sit correctly within each surface.

Now I'm positioning the shield group on the arm with a slight Y rotation so it faces outward naturally, then adding scattered scratch details as thin dark boxes across the breastplate, pauldrons, helm, and shield to give a worn, battle-used look.

Next I'm working out the surcoat panel dimensions and adding gold trim boxes along its top and bottom edges, placing the griffin emblem centered on the chest, and positioning a leather belt with a gold buckle at the waist. I'll finish with a dent detail on the helm and breastplate before returning the completed root group.

Before finalizing, I'm double-checking that the sword, pauldrons, and shoulder details are positioned correctly, adding a couple of small gold torus rings and dots as filigree accents on the pauldrons, and confirming shadow flags are set properly throughout. Now I'm ready to write out the complete, final code for the knight model.
